title: Short Title, Commencement and Application
old_text: IPC Sections 1 to 5 defined the title, extent across India, punishment of offences committed within or beyond India, extraterritorial operation, and savings for certain local/special laws.
new_text: This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. It applies to every person within India and extraterritorially to Indian citizens abroad, ships/aircraft registered in India, and computer targets in India, saving certain military and special laws.
punishment_new: General jurisdictional application rules, explicitly covering cyber attacks on Indian computer resources.
explanation: Section 1 consolidates IPC Sections 1 to 5 into a single comprehensive title and territorial jurisdiction clause. It expressly codifies extraterritorial jurisdiction over cyber offences targeting Indian computer resources.

title: Definitions
old_text: Scattered definitions across IPC Sections 6 to 30 (act, person, gender, public servant, movable property, electronic record, valuable security, etc.).
new_text: Consolidates 39 core definitions in alphabetical order, including act, child, court, document, electronic record, gender, good faith, government, injury, judge, public servant, and valuable security.
explanation: BNS Section 2 unifies dozens of previously scattered IPC definition sections into a single alphabetical section. It modernizes terms like 'document' and 'electronic record' and defines 'child' consistently.

title: General Explanations and Common Intention
old_text: IPC Sections 32-38 governed acts done by several persons, omissions, and common intention (Section 34).
new_text: Section 3 sets out general interpretive principles. Sub-section (5) retains the classic rule that when a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of common intention, each is liable as if done by him alone.
punishment_new: Constructive joint criminal liability retained under sub-section 3(5).
explanation: The famed common intention principle of IPC Section 34 is now placed in Section 3(5). Subsections (1) to (9) integrate principles of joint liability, omissions, and cooperative criminal acts.
